title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Large Language Models on Mental Illnesses

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3.1 ('standard parameters (e.g., temperature 0)') and Sec. 3.8 (response length limit of 2 tokens for all models); top_p assumed

task.subset_rule: paper-defined: fair (class-balanced) random sample of 1,000 posts = 250 per severity level, seeded 20260907 (hook load_items; Sec. 3.3 / 3.6)
task.approximation: Different 1,000-post balanced sample (IDs unpublished); SEV-4 wording transcribed from the Figure 1 image, block separators and post placement (post appended after a blank line) assumed.

items.source: github.com/usmaann/Depression_Severity_Dataset, file Reddit_depression_dataset.csv (3,553 rows verified: minimum 2,587 / mild 290 / moderate 394 / severe 282)

prompt.user_template:
As a psychologist, analyze the provided social media post(s).
Is the poster depressed?
On a scale of 0 to 3, how likely is this?
Label Representations:
0. No depressive symptoms
1. Mild depressive symptoms
2. Moderate depressive symptoms
3. Severe depressive symptoms
(Answer only with a number between 0 and 3 without explaining your reasoning. If the post is unclear, choose the most probable label without any extra explanation.)
(Please return only the label and no other text.)

{post}
prompt.source_location: Figure 1 (SEV-4 = SEV-1 + label representations + response formatting + repetition line; transcribed from the PDF image, arXiv 2409.15687v2 p. 13)
prompt.verbatim: full for the prompt text (Figure 1 image transcribed); block separators and the post placement are not printed

placeholders_prose.post: items.post (hook load_items: the Reddit post text)

output.parse: hook: integers in the reply; exactly one integer within 0-3 -> level, else invalid (Sec. 3.7)
output.postprocess: invalid responses reported separately and counted as incorrect

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: hook: BA (%) = mean per-class recall over the four severity levels (Sec. 3.6; invalid = wrong); MAE over valid replies printed (secondary, 0.805)

notes: The CSV spells the lowest level 'minimum' (paper: 'minimal'). Table 5/Figure 1 show SEV-1..SEV-4 differ by numbered list, ambiguity clause and repetition line only. || [hooks_2 2026-09-07] SEV-4 transcribed from the Figure 1 image; balanced sampling per Sec. 3.6; 2-token limit per Sec. 3.8; BA = mean per-class recall; prepare verified (1,000 items x 3 seeds).
hook: harness/tierb/hooks/W4403786592.py: load_items (balanced 250/class seeded), parse (single integer 0-3), score (balanced accuracy, weighted per-item)
